headline: Bitkom: 57% of German firms now use AI — and a third fear for their existence; China blasts AI-slowdown push as Cold War tactic; Vega-C FLEX/Sentinel-3C set for 03:21 CEST liftoff.

stories.title: Bitkom: majority of German companies now use AI

facts.text: Bitkom (14 Sep, n=603 firms ≥20 employees): 57% already use AI — up from 36% a year ago and 20% two years ago; another 38% plan or discuss it; only 4% say AI is “no topic”.
Depth lag: among AI users, none claim full potential use; just 3% say they exploit it rather strongly; 28% little, 59% not at all. Wintergerst: “breadth arrived — the real work starts now.”
Anxiety rises with adoption: 34% fear AI threatens their firm’s existence (23% last year); 61% say firms without AI have no future; 91% call AI the most important future tech.

Where it pays: 66% of users say competitive position improved; 48% sped internal processes; 45% see measurable contribution to success. Top brakes for users: data protection (66%), legal uncertainty (56%).
AI Act backlash: 37% expect to be in-scope as users (23% YoY); of those affected/checking, 89% expect high implementation effort; 66% of all firms say the Act brings more harm than good.
Agents next: of firms using/planning/discussing AI, 11% already run agents, 29% plan, 31% discuss; only 24% say agents are not a topic.

stories.whyItMatters: Hard German survey evidence that AI crossed majority adoption while existential fear and AI-Act friction climbed — useful counterweight to the weekend’s frontier-lab pacing drama.

stories.title: China hits AI-slowdown push as Cold War play; Altman fleshes out pacing

facts.text: Global Times editorial (Mon): Amodei’s weekend “pace the frontier” essay is a “Cold War playbook” to curb China’s AI via tech barriers/regulatory monopoly — “hypocritical and short-sighted.”
Straits Times/GT: essay (Sat) later endorsed by OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Elon Musk; Amodei also urged tighter US chip controls and action on alleged Chinese-lab distillation.

CNBC: Altman’s Monday X post welcomes a US federal frontier-safety framework and independent auditors; warns of losing “control of the future to AI” or power concentrating in one person/company — pacing ≠ stopping.
Trump brushed off slowdown calls (per ST/CNBC); China’s MFA Mon urged an open/inclusive approach — confrontation disrupts AI governance.
Calendar: US–China frontier AI safety talks eyed mid-September; Trump–Xi summit listed for 24 Sep.

stories.whyItMatters: The weekend lab consensus meets a hard Beijing rebuttal on Monday — pacing now sits inside great-power competition, not just safety blogs.

stories.title: Nadella: superintelligence only if it helps humanity — and stays under human control

facts.text: ComputerBase (14 Sep): Satya Nadella on X (13 Sep) — any pursuit of superintelligence is “not worth pursuing” if the AI does not help humanity and remain under human control.
He welcomes deliberate frontier pacing / embedded evaluators, but wants already-useful AI diffused faster across countries, communities, and companies — closed and open-source both thriving.
Enterprises must keep control of unique/tacit knowledge and model weights (“continuous learning loop”) rather than depend on one provider; governance “cannot be controlled by a handful of entities.”
Microsoft to publish a Code of Conduct for first-party MAI models for public consultation (Nadella said “tomorrow” from the Sunday post — i.e. Mon 14 Sep).

stories.whyItMatters: Microsoft’s CEO joins the weekend pacing chorus with a sharper split: slow the frontier, accelerate diffusion, and keep enterprises (and humans) in the loop.

stories.title: Beijing bans private drone possession after June tower crash

facts.text: heise (citing Bloomberg / Beijing daily): private possession or storage of drones or drone parts in Beijing will be banned from 14 Nov; owners get ~2 months to remove devices from the city or hand them in.
Buyback: government offers up to 3,000 yuan (~€390) per surrendered drone depending on model.
Beijing declared controlled airspace barring non-commercial aviation; authorities also plan tighter airspace checks within ~300 km of the capital.

Trigger: 26 Jun light-sport aircraft deliberately struck the 108-storey CITIC Tower — pilot killed, 13 injured; near-miss with airliner reported. heise: possession ban goes beyond city flight bans in Paris/Rome/Vienna.

stories.whyItMatters: A capital-wide ownership ban — not just no-fly zones — is a sharp escalation in urban UAS control after a high-rise crash.

stories.title: Vega-C VV30: FLEX + Sentinel-3C encapsulated for 03:21 CEST liftoff

facts.text: ESA (14 Sep): FLEX and Copernicus Sentinel-3C are encapsulated in the Vega-C fairing at Kourou; launch tonight — 15 Sep 03:21 CEST (14 Sep 22:21 local).
Sequence: Sentinel-3C deploys first, then FLEX from the Vespa+R adapter after launcher manoeuvres. Live coverage starts 02:50 CEST.
FLEX (Earth Explorer) maps plant fluorescence / vegetation health from ~814 km; Sentinel-3C continues ocean/land/ice/atmosphere monitoring with 3A/3B.
Flight VV30: Avio is prime contractor and launch-service operator for this Vega-C mission.

stories.whyItMatters: Material update on this morning’s FLEX tip — Europe’s dual Earth-observation stack is on the pad for overnight liftoff.
